_info: Vocabulario en flashcards. Cada mazo tiene sus tarjetas: 'term' (inglés), 'meaning' (español), 'definition' (inglés simple), 'example' (frase de ejemplo) y opcionalmente 'note'. Los 'id' de tarjetas deben ser únicos.

decks.title: Negocios y agenda
decks.description: El idioma de los calendarios, las reuniones y los pendientes. Clave para asistente ejecutiva.

cards.meaning: reservar un espacio en el calendario
cards.definition: to reserve time in a calendar for a specific task
cards.example: I'll block time on Friday morning for you to review the board deck.
cards.note: También: «Can you block 30 minutes for me?»

cards.meaning: pasar una reunión para más tarde
cards.definition: to move a meeting to a later time or date
cards.example: Can we push our 2 p.m. to Thursday?
cards.note: Lo contrario: «pull it forward» / «move it up» (adelantarla).

cards.meaning: con dos compromisos a la misma hora
cards.definition: having two appointments at the same time
cards.example: Mr. Lee is double-booked at 10, so I moved the vendor call to 11.

cards.definition: one right after another, with no break
cards.example: She has back-to-back meetings until 4, so let's send her a summary instead.

cards.meaning: una hora de salida que no se puede pasar
cards.definition: a fixed time when you must leave a meeting
cards.example: Just a heads-up: I have a hard stop at 3.

cards.definition: a tentative calendar entry that holds a time slot
cards.example: I sent a placeholder for Tuesday at 9 until the client confirms.

cards.meaning: reunión corta para ponerse al día
cards.definition: a short meeting to align on status or next steps
cards.example: Do you have 15 minutes for a quick sync before the client call?

cards.meaning: hablar brevemente para ponerse al día
cards.definition: to briefly contact someone to check in
cards.example: Let's touch base on Monday about the shipment schedule.

cards.meaning: incluir a alguien en la conversación o el email
cards.definition: to include someone in a conversation or email thread
cards.example: I'll loop in Ana from Finance so she can approve the invoice.

cards.definition: to return to a topic later
cards.example: Let's circle back on the budget once we have the supplier's quote.

cards.meaning: señalarlo, avisar de un posible problema
cards.definition: to point out an issue so others notice it
cards.example: If the customs broker needs more documents, just flag it and I'll follow up.

cards.definition: the time or energy someone has available to take on work
cards.example: Do you have the bandwidth to help with the travel arrangements this week?

cards.meaning: quitarte esa tarea de encima, encargarme yo
cards.definition: to take responsibility for a task so someone else doesn't have to
cards.example: I can take the expense reports off your plate so you can focus on the proposal.
cards.note: «plate» = lo que tenés en tu plato, tus pendientes.

cards.definition: to be the main person responsible for coordinating something
cards.example: I'll run point on the offsite logistics: venue, travel and catering.

cards.meaning: al final del día (end of day)
cards.definition: end of day — by the end of the working day
cards.example: I'll send you the updated tracker by EOD.

cards.meaning: al final de la semana (end of week)
cards.definition: end of week — usually by Friday
cards.example: Can we have the final numbers by EOW?

cards.meaning: fuera de la oficina (out of office)
cards.definition: out of office — on vacation, sick or away
cards.example: I'll be OOO on Monday, but Carlos can help with anything urgent.

cards.meaning: al cierre de la jornada (close of business)
cards.definition: close of business — the end of the official working day
cards.example: The supplier needs the signed PO by COB today.
cards.note: Ojo con husos horarios: aclará «COB Madrid time» o «COB Eastern».

decks.title: Verbos de logro
decks.description: Los verbos que muestran lo que VOS hiciste. Para tu CV, LinkedIn y respuestas STAR.

cards.definition: helped someone do their work or reach a goal
cards.example: I supported three regional managers with scheduling and travel.

cards.definition: dealt with something successfully
cards.example: I handled 60 to 80 calls a day from US customers on loan accounts.

cards.definition: was in charge of something and made it work
cards.example: I managed purchase orders with suppliers in five countries.

cards.meaning: hice de enlace con, coordiné con
cards.definition: worked as the connection between two people or groups
cards.example: I liaised with customs brokers and the warehouse to clear shipments on time.
cards.note: Se pronuncia /liˈeɪzd/. Muy valorado en roles de asistente y logística.

cards.definition: organized people or tasks so they work together
cards.example: I coordinated deliveries from Japan and Germany for the same week.

cards.definition: found a solution to a problem
cards.example: I resolved billing disputes on the first call in most cases.

cards.definition: checked something carefully to make sure it was correct
cards.example: I reviewed every commercial invoice before it went to customs.

cards.definition: confirmed that information was accurate
cards.example: I verified HS codes and quantities in TICA before submitting the declaration.

cards.definition: made a process simpler and more efficient
cards.example: I streamlined the import checklist, which cut documentation errors.

cards.definition: watched over and directed work (past of oversee)
cards.example: I oversaw the onboarding of two new agents on the healthcare account.

cards.meaning: me hice cargo de, asumí como propio
cards.definition: took full responsibility for something
cards.example: I took ownership of the escalated cases and followed each one until it closed.

cards.definition: produced or achieved what was expected
cards.example: I delivered the monthly import report on time every month.

decks.title: Social y small talk
decks.description: Frases cortas que te hacen sonar natural en el pasillo, en Slack y antes de una reunión.

cards.definition: a casual way to say hello and ask how someone is
cards.example: Hey Sarah, how's it going? — Good, busy week! You?
cards.note: No espera una respuesta larga: «Good, thanks! You?» alcanza.

cards.meaning: ¿Tenés planes para el fin de semana?
cards.definition: a common Friday small-talk question
cards.example: Any plans for the weekend? — Just relaxing. Maybe a trip to the beach.

cards.definition: I understand and agree with your reasoning
cards.example: So we push the meeting until the quote arrives? — That makes sense.

cards.definition: I accept your point, even if I didn't think of it first
cards.example: We can't approve it until Finance signs off. — Fair enough.

cards.definition: it's fine; no problem
cards.example: Sorry I'm a few minutes late! — No worries, we just started.

cards.definition: I'm extremely busy
cards.example: I'm swamped today — can we touch base tomorrow morning?

cards.meaning: Se me olvidó / Se me pasó
cards.definition: I forgot (in a polite, natural way)
cards.example: Sorry, it slipped my mind — I'll send the agenda right now.

cards.definition: an informal way to admit a small mistake
cards.example: My bad, I sent you the old version. Here's the right one.
cards.note: Informal: entre colegas sí, con un cliente o un VP mejor «My mistake».

cards.term: Off the top of my head
cards.definition: from memory, without checking
cards.example: Off the top of my head, I think the container arrives on the 14th — let me confirm.

cards.meaning: Ya me encargo / En eso estoy
cards.definition: I'm taking care of it right now
cards.example: The client needs the contract signed today. — I'm on it.
